## Why visit

An unusually complete match for this trip: a small independent local that takes cask seriously and still rewards sitting and talking. Four compact drinking spaces, interwar glass and surviving snug details give it a different scale from Liverpool’s palatial show pubs. Its own site describes a music-free pub with six cask choices. Make this an anchor for the Georgian-quarter walk, allowing time for a second beer if the cellar and conversation invite it. Its enduring Good Beer Guide history is useful context, rather than a substitute for assessing the pint in front of you.

## Beer

Six cask ales advertised by the pub; CAMRA records regular bitters and changing guests. CAMRA names Tetley Bitter, Timothy Taylor Landlord and Fyne Ales Jarl as regular cask beers; changing suppliers include Colbier. Reconfirm trading and the selection amid the reported sale.

## Food

The pub advertises locally baked hot pies; a useful small meal rather than a restaurant booking.

## Plan the visit

Small rooms can fill quickly. No music is advertised. Ask staff before photographing occupied snugs.

**Getting there:** Roscoe Street; combine on foot with the Dispensary, Grapes and Hope Street pubs.
